title: Outlook for Mac: DLP policy tips and override
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, disabled-by-default tip UI, Cloud Policy route and override command are supported. It accurately reports Microsoft's conflicting Mac support documentation and the remaining Mac-specific gaps. The override portal path needs a minor extension to end at the option itself.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft 365 Apps admin center route reaches the Mac policy tip setting through the Cloud Policy configuration wizard.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. ... On the Policy configurations page, select Create. ... Start with the basics ... Choose the scope ... On the Configure Settings page, select the policies

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn PowerShell or Graph operation configuring these Cloud Policy settings is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Cloud Policy service Microsoft 365 policy settings PowerShell Microsoft Graph API configure; Cloud Policy PowerShell policy configurations; Cloud Policy Graph settings API. Opened Cloud Policy overview; results document portal configuration and auditing, not a settings operation.

claims.claim: The printed Purview portal route reaches Policy tips in the documented oversharing rule creation procedure.
claims.quote: Select Full directory under Admin units. ... Select only the Exchange email location. ... On the Define policy settings page, select Create or customize advanced DLP rules. ... Select Create rule. ... Set the User notifications toggle to On. ... Select Policy tips
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path to 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom > Admin units > Full directory > Exchange email > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > User notifications > Policy tips > Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only) > Allow override from M365 services'. Keep the note that this is the oversharing procedure, not a Mac-specific route. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-osp-get-started.

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <rule name> -Policy <policy name> -BlockAccess $true -NotifyAllowOverride WithJustification creates a rule with justification-based override.
claims.quote: The NotifyAllowOverride parameter specifies the notification override options when the conditions of the rule are met. ... WithJustification: Allows overrides with justification.

claims.claim: The oversharing procedure locates the dialog option and Allow override from M365 services in the policy tip settings.
claims.quote: Select Policy tips > Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only). ... If already selected, uncheck the Allow override from M365 services option.

claims.claim: Microsoft also requires an appropriate BlockAccessScope value for the described override configuration.
claims.quote: make sure BlockAccess is set to true and BlockAccessScope has appropriate value. Otherwise, the policy tip comes up but the user doesn't find an option to override the email with justification.

claims.claim: The Mac reference gives no separate Mac portal path to override.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac DLP policy tips Cloud Policy rule evaluation permissions identity automated actions override configuration Purview path. Opened the platform reference, notifications guide and oversharing guide; no separate Mac-specific override portal route found.

claims.claim: The user chooses whether to use an allowed override.
claims.quote: Depending on how you configure the policy tips in the DLP policy, people can choose to ignore the policy tip, override the policy with or without a business justification, or report a false positive.

claims.claim: DLP rules determine notification text and show tips for matching content.
claims.quote: For each rule in a DLP policy, you can configure policy tips to: ... Notify the person that the content conflicts with a DLP policy ... You can use the default text ... or enter custom text
